title: 6 Signs You’re A Pushover
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes being perceived as a pushover as a common blind spot: students recognize it clearly, but the teacher often does not. He lists six telltale signs, including uncertainty about what actually breaks class rules, students arguing over consequences, disrespectful behavior, catching oneself trying to verbally convince students to behave, students acting as though the teacher isn't present, and quiet resentment that surfaces even in well-behaved students who feel unprotected. He clarifies that being perceived as a pushover doesn't reflect a lack of personal strength, but rather insufficient clarity about rule boundaries. The remedy is deciding precisely where those boundaries lie and then boldly, consistently following through, which he claims can reverse the pushover perception within about a week.

Clarifies that being perceived as a pushover is a perception problem, not evidence of a lack of personal strength.
Argues the fix — clarifying rule boundaries and following through boldly — can reverse the perception within about a week.
quotes: This is a big problem because unless you’re aware of your weaknesses, you can’t address them. You’ll continue to struggle and not know why.
If you’re uncertain about what does and doesn’t constitute transgressing your rules, then you’ll waffle when it comes to enforcing them.
In fact, trying to convince students to behave only reinforces the image they have of you as weak and easily manipulated.
You’ll have to raise your voice and repeat yourself just to be heard. Just getting through lessons becomes an exercise in frustration.
Being viewed by students as a pushover doesn’t mean that you’re not a strong person. Just deciding to become a teacher and showing up every day is proof that you are strong.
Commit to it mind, body, and soul and the perception of you as a pushover will be gone in a week.
